rubrics.criterion: The cohesive fetcher-construction pack (crate name and version, repo URL, target triple, package metadata, template-rendering values, the shared repo-info cache, and the signature policy) is carried by one owning abstraction, so that no remaining constructor or helper in the resolved patch still threads the whole pack as a flat list of bare parameters.
rubrics.rationale: This pack is the exact relation the task asks the solver to recognise; collapsing it into a single value is the central resolution, not a side effect.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not replace the bare group with a positional tuple or type alias that re-exposes the same elements positionally at every call site, leaving the clump merely rebatched rather than owned.
rubrics.rationale: For this fetcher-construction pack a bare tuple would preserve positional coupling and would still repeat the group across signatures, so it is not a resolving abstraction.

rubrics.criterion: All six participating sites move to the abstraction: the fetcher trait construction surface, both concrete fetcher constructors, the per-target orchestration helper, the bin-collection helper, and the bin-file constructor each accept the pack as the one value rather than as expanded elements.
rubrics.rationale: The constructor group appears in exactly these five responsibility areas; a repair that skips any of them leaves a stranded carrier and the relation undiminished.

rubrics.criterion: Every call site in crates/binstalk and crates/binstalk-fetchers that previously built a fetcher or forwarded the pack is migrated to construct and pass the abstraction, so no caller is left assembling the old positional group.
rubrics.rationale: The resolution loop and the two fetchers mutually construct one another; co-migration of all call sites is what makes the abstraction load-bearing here.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not strand a half-migrated constructor that still accepts the expanded pack alongside the abstraction (dual signatures), keeping two occupancy forms alive for the same construction facts.
rubrics.rationale: Because the fetcher trait surface is shared, a dual-signature constructor would let some call sites keep the clump and quietly re-introduce the smell.

rubrics.criterion: Injected scaffolding that existed only to pass the clump element-by-element is removed once redundant -- for example the per-constructor dead fields retained purely to satisfy the shared construction signature -- rather than left behind under suppression attributes.
rubrics.rationale: QuickInstall gained fields marked dead_code solely to match the expanded constructor; once the pack is owned elsewhere those fields become pure smell residue worth removing.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave behind now-unused intermediate structs, type aliases, or forwarding helpers whose sole purpose was the pre-repair threading of the pack.
rubrics.rationale: Orphaned threaders would reintroduce the recurring group by another route and would obscure whether the abstraction genuinely owns the facts.

rubrics.criterion: Repository behavior is preserved: the workspace builds and the existing test suite passes with the same outcome count as the injected baseline, with no test removed or skipped to mask a regression.
rubrics.rationale: This refactor concerns constructor plumbing across fetchers; the existing fetcher and resolution tests are the precise regression guard for the facts being moved.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not drop semantics the pack must carry: the per-crate repo-info OnceCell (get_or_try_init sharing across fetchers) and the template-values accessor still behave identically across the trait and both fetchers.
rubrics.rationale: The repo-info cache and the template-values plumbing are load-bearing behavior bundled into the pack; a restructuring that folds them in but loses the sharing regresses resolution.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not gratuitously broaden the public API surface or change the visibility or return type of the Fetcher trait or its constructors beyond what carrying the abstraction requires.
rubrics.rationale: Fetcher is part of the cross-crate fetcher interface; unrelated visibility churn there would change the contract external crates rely on, beyond the data-clump scope.
